Black October update: 124 new cyber incidents

25 VERY serious incidents (among the biggest of a normal *year*)

- Hospital emergency rooms closed
- Schools closed across Europe
- Rogue AI agents infiltrated banks
- Flights cancelled across the US
- Boil water advisory issued in South Carolina

*** YEAR- LEVEL INCIDENTS (in a typical year, these would be among the biggest incidents of the year):

1. Germany: hackers shut down a hospital's emergency room. Days later it's still closed, and emergencies go elsewhere.

2. South Carolina: a mystery power outage at the main water plant broke its main water lines. Taps ran dry for over 100,000 customers, about a quarter million had to boil their water, and a college sent its students home. Possible cyberattack.

3. Europe: more than 8,000 bomb threats, mostly by email, have hit schools, flights and TV stations in a month. In Italy, 6,300 schools got one in a single day and 1,800 more the next, as parents raced to get their kids. This week police cleared 20 schools in one Spanish city. No bombs have been found.

4. US flights: three days after switching on a new AI air-traffic system nationwide, the FAA had to stop every departing flight in America for hours in a suspected AI-related failure, the longest ground stop in 25 years. About 15,000 flights were disrupted. The FBI's cyber teams are assisting. Panicked shoppers bought out most of Costco's big generators online.

5. Microsoft: in another suspected AI-related outage, Outlook and Teams crashed for a day in over 70 countries. Jails couldn't release prisoners and hospitals went back to paper. At a German theme park, alarm emails never arrived, and chlorine in the pool hurt 15 guests.

6. New Orleans: a tanker lost steering and crashed into a riverboat carrying about 129 passengers plus crew, capsizing it. Passengers fell into the river; 32 were hurt, none killed. Possible cyberattack.

7. US: a ransomware gang hit Vanderbilt, one of America's top universities, which told everyone on campus, including 14,000 students, to shut down their devices.

8. US: Chase and Bank of America went down and Zelle payments failed. Bank executives reportedly told Congress that rushed fixes for AI-found security holes caused it.

9. US: the NSA lost its classified network for days and reportedly told Congress rushed fixes for AI-found security holes were to blame. Then the White House fired its top cybersecurity official. Sen. Hawley: "If this is all a coincidence, it's like the greatest coincidence in the history of the world."

10. US: payroll giant Workday, used by 11,500 employers including Walmart and Target, crashed. Possible cyberattack.

11. Apple Pay, iCloud and Apple Support went down for most of a day. Possible cyberattack.

12. AI: an AI "agent swarm" got past two-factor logins, stole a company's data and locked up its entire system in 14 minutes, an ex-NSA hacker fighting it told CNN: "Never seen anything that fast before."

13. North Korea: hackers lured people into fake Zoom and Teams calls, secretly filmed them through their webcams, then used the footage to fool their friends on the next call. They stole over $400 million in crypto. The FBI seized over 900 of the videos.

14. Freezers: France formally blamed Iran for hacking freezers in up to 700 supermarkets and cranking them to about 50°C; stores dumped food and some caught fire. In Britain, workers raced to pull tens of thousands of fridges off the internet before the next wave. Suspected AI: the US Treasury Secretary says the hackers used a Chinese AI model.

15. AI: Arizona opened a criminal investigation into OpenAI over the "apparent infiltration of banks by rogue AI agents." California is already suing OpenAI: hundreds of its agents broke out of testing and hacked Hugging Face, and OpenAI told the state it lost control of its agents over 80 times.

16. Germany: hackers reportedly booby-trapped an update for drones the German army flies, and the army grounded them.

17. A security breach forced the US Department of Agriculture to shut down systems, including the ones that pay America's farmers.

18. The European Union was hacked: the European Commission blames an "AI-generated cyber campaign," which reportedly disrupted its staff payroll, leave and medical-claims systems for over 10 days.

19. AI: for the first time, Google caught an AI hacking websites and stealing data entirely on its own, with no human involved.

20. AI: researchers say a jailbroken AI agent hacked a European phone company for two weeks while its human boss barely checked in, reportedly reaching millions of patient records.

21. Hackers likely stole up to 37.6 million customer records from Nitori, Japan's biggest furniture chain: like 3 in 10 people in Japan.

22. Hackers broke into Rakuten Securities, one of Japan's biggest online brokers, and got data on up to 15.7 million accounts, some with incomes and bank details.

23. Hackers hit Expedia and claim to have 800 million records.

24. Bulgaria uncovered the longest and largest cyber-spying operation ever recorded against its government.

25. Hackers leaked what they say are Russia's secret records of its war dead: 450,000 people.

*** MONTH-LEVEL INCIDENTS (In a typical month, these would be among the biggest incidents):

26. Hackers stole more than a million credit and debit cards by infecting 782 store card terminals in over 20 countries, mostly in Brazil.

27. Belgium: four hospitals went back to pen and paper when their patient records went dark for a day. Brussels' university hospital canceled operations and sent ambulances elsewhere. Possible cyberattack.

28. US: a cyber incident has knocked a New Hampshire hospital offline for over a week, and emergency ambulances now go elsewhere.

29. US: a "potential security threat" forced Vermont to shut off the system most of its police use to dispatch officers and keep records.

30. US: a suspected hack knocked courts offline across California and in Las Vegas. Judges canceled hearings, and authorities had to free one defendant (then re-arrested him) because his hearing couldn't happen in time.

31. Spain: ransomware hit the national sea-rescue service during a record wave of migrant boats, forcing it to shut down the system that tracks emergencies.

32. Japan: ransomware silenced a city's 229 disaster-warning loudspeakers and the emergency radios in its homes.

33. Netherlands: suspected jamming scrambled GPS for about 80 airliners, and seven struggled to land at Amsterdam's airport. Experts think Russia is stepping up its hybrid war.

34. France: hackers stole a gold dealer's customer list. Then fake police officers showed up at customers' homes and took their gold: at least €765,000 so far.

35. The Polish government came under cyberattack and took its national website for dealing with the state offline. The minister says the plan was bigger: to paralyze public offices in December.

36. Hackers hit suppliers of Visa, Mastercard and JPMorgan Chase and likely got some customers' names and emails.

37. Hackers stole 72,000 passport photos from Taiwan's foreign ministry.

38. Pro-Russian hackers posted Italy's foreign minister's phone numbers and are offering money for more on him and his family.

39. A ransomware gang claims it hacked shipping giant Maersk.

Also serious:

40. US: a cyberattack shut down every school in an Ohio district for a day.

41. US: 911 went dead across an Ohio county into a second day, amid a statewide AT&T 911 outage. Possible cyberattack.

42. Norwegian Air told 5,000 customers to block their payment cards after hackers struck.

43. Hackers cut phone and internet to 8,000 German homes and offices.

44. Phone scammers conned a Moscow woman out of a record $5 million in cash.

45. Crypto: a breach left 44,000 Keplr wallets wide open, and thieves and rescuers raced to empty them: about $6 million drained.

46. Ukraine: police and the FBI arrested four members of a gang that posed as IT support with AI-generated voices and extorted $40.5 million from 28 companies.

47. Tokyo: police arrested a man driving a fake cell tower through its famous Ginza district. It knocked over 10,000 phones off their network, apparently to blast scam texts.

Also hacked:
- Brazil's National Treasury
- Japan's flagship supercomputer, Fugaku
- Brazil's state bank Caixa (7.6 million clients)
- Chip giant TSMC
- Uber
- Sony Life, Yamada Denki and Tokyo's Skyliner airport train

- AI coding app Cursor
- Code on the BBC, CNN and Zoom websites
- Links in Trump's X posts
- The city of Osaka
- Colombia's intelligence agency (reportedly)
- Ukraine's state news agency
- Charleston County, South Carolina
- South Portland, Maine (suspected)
- A California hospital
- Brazil's Port of Santos
- London's Oyster photocards (265,000 people)
- 22.7 million French drivers' records (claimed)
- Germany's AfD party donors
- Doraemon publisher Shogakukan
- Malaysia's Bank Rakyat
- Polish payments firm Autopay
- Bitcoin firm Luxor
- 12 Indian lenders ($7 million)
- Equinor, one of Europe's biggest gas suppliers

Also went down (possible cyberattacks):
- United Airlines
- Charles Schwab
- AT&T's network
- Marriott's website and app
- Florida's driver's license system
- Mississippi's unemployment system
- Russia's internet, banking apps and government services
- Pakistan's internet
- Lloyds Bank's app
- Nuremberg's main train station
- Geneva's biggest hospital
- Phones at UPMC and WVU Medicine hospitals
- Power for 106,000 people around Bolzano, Italy
- Emergency numbers on France's Mayotte island
- Scott County, Iowa's government systems

Plus 30 smaller ones.

The Growing Threat of Tech Censorship: Stefan Molyneux Speaks at the European Union Parliament

Stefan Molyneux speaks at the EU Parliament 31 Jan 2019.

- Tommy Robinson banned by Twitter and PayPal
- Laura Loomer banned by Twitter
- Republican consultant R.C. Maxwell banned by Twitter
- Carl Benjamin (“Sargon of Akkad”) banned by Patreon
- Robert Spencer banned by Patreon following pressure by credit card companies.
- Candace Owens suspended by Twitter
- James Woods suspended for 30 days by Twitter
- I, Hypocrite, focused on far-left hate speech banned by Facebook
- Avi Yemini, a Jewish-Australian IDF veteran and conservative activist was banned by Facebook
- Mohammed Tawhidi, an anti-extremist imam: banned by Facebook
- The Babylon Bee, a conservative humor site: threatened with suspension by Facebook
- Terrence K. Williams: suspended by Facebook
- Gavin McInnes: banned by Twitter and Facebook
- Alex Jones/Infowars: banned by Facebook, Twitter, Apple Podcasts, Google Play, Spotify, Pinterest, and YouTube
- Over 800 alternative news accounts were banned by Facebook shortly before the US midterms

- Tech companies have invested hundreds of millions in “news” media.
- Facebook and Apple, YouTube have all announced that they will directly fund handpicked “authoritative news sources.”
- These sources will then be promoted to their users without ads.
- Google, YouTube’s parent company, has committed a budget of $300 million to pay for “quality journalism.”
- YouTube has committed $25 million to paying for “news.”
- YouTube has also reported that it will “prominently surface authoritative sources” for users. (again, promotion with no ads)
- Jan 2018, Facebook code changes pushed “establishment” news sources to the top of engagement – CNN at the top.
- Mark Zuckerberg’s stated goal was to promote “high-quality news” that “helps build a sense of common ground.”
- The “trusted sources” ranking – any conservative outlets?
- Zuckerberg’s example of “good trustworthy journalism”: The New York Times.
- Facebook announced it would partner with 80 unnamed publications to create “exclusive news content” ahead of the 2018 US midterm elections.
- Facebook said it planned to directly fund news programming, such as shows from CNN’s Anderson Cooper and http://Mic.com.
- These outlets often parrot the “Russia Collusion” conspiracy.
- Fact: Google CEO Sundar Pichai told Congress that his company could only find $4,700 in ad spending from Russia-linked accounts in 2016, the Trump election year.
- National Review: “Private interests that closed deals with Vladimir Putin and his agents — thanks to then–secretary of state Hillary Clinton’s public favors — gave the Clinton Foundation between $152 million and $173 million.”
- 36,809 times the spending.
- Tech workers overwhelmingly support Democrats. In 2018, just over 1% of the $15 million sent to candidates went to Republicans. Where is the diversity?
- 23% went to Democrats – are tech people above bias?
- “Saudi money is already behind many of the biggest tech startups in the US, including Lyft, Uber and Magic Leap. Saudi Arabia’s massive $45 billion check to SoftBank’s Vision Fund, the largest venture fund of all time, means Saudi money will likely be part of the biggest pool of venture money for years to come. The Vision Fund has made at least 26 investments including into Slack, WeWork, GM Cruise, and other brand names.
- “Over the last five years, Quid estimates Saudi investors have directly participated in investment rounds totaling at least $6.2 billion.

Will rapid AI capability improvements translate into runaway economic growth?

Economists Alex Imas and Tyler Cowen are skeptical. In this conversation with a16z's Erik Torenberg, they cover:

- Why smarter models can't automatically overcome economic bottlenecks
- Why slow-moving institutions can limit AI's impact on the economy
- How competition between AI labs is making powerful models cheaper to use
- Why AI's benefits to consumers could be much larger than GDP captures
- Why scientific advances and longer lifespans could be among AI's biggest benefits

- The Polish Solana Ecosystem Report

Why This Matters?
Poland is quietly becoming one of the most important Solana builder hubs on the planet.

While the crypto world watches the US and Asia, a cohort of world-class engineers in Warsaw, Krakow, and Wroclaw are shipping production grade DeFi protocols, ZK infrastructure, DePIN hardware, AI trading tools, and cross-chain execution layers, all on Solana.

--

The Solana Context

Before the projects: understand the battlefield. Solana in 2025–2026 by the numbers:
1. $2.5B+ DEX volume per day
2. $9–11B DeFi TVL
3. 88M+ daily transactions
4. 2,100+ active dApps (↑54% YoY)
5. $15B+ stablecoin supply
6. $3.5B DePIN market cap, 240K active nodes
7. $1B+ perps volume per day (Q1 2025)
8. 100% uptime for 18+ consecutive months
9. Jupiter Perps: 79.2% market share in on-chain derivatives

This is the environment Polish builders are launching into.

Firedancer:
Jump Crypto's next-gen validator client targeting 1M TPS is on the horizon, which will directly expand capacity for every transaction-intensive protocol on this list.

--

Why Poland?
1. Poland's fintech sector grew from 167 companies in 2018 to 383 in 2025. That's +129% in seven years.
2. Between mid-2023 and mid-2024, Poland, Czechia, and Hungary recorded nearly $500B in combined on-chain inflows.
3. Polish engineers have deep backgrounds in mathematics, cryptography, and systems programming, the exact disciplines that matter most in blockchain development. Rust, the language of Solana smart contracts, is a natural fit for a country that produces elite competitive programmers.
4. The EU's MiCA regulation gives Polish crypto projects a structural compliance advantage: a single legal framework covering 27 countries and 450 million people. No offshore island incorporation required. No regulatory arbitrage. Just a clean slate to build institutional-grade products.
5. Warsaw's Next Block Expo draws 1,700+ attendees. The Warsaw University of Technology now teaches blockchain at the academic level.

The talent pipeline is real. The regulatory moat is real. The community is real.

--

The 8 Projects

1. @NeonyExchange: Perpetual DEX

Mission:
Crypto can be fair again. Not just for VCs and whales. Neony is a multi-collateral perpetual exchange built on a dedicated high-performance Layer 1. 

It supports spot and perp trading across crypto, synthetic stocks, and forex - all from a single account interface, with gasless trading and cross-collateral support.

What makes it different:
1. No VC allocations. No private deals. Ever.
2. Proof of Fairness: An on-chain transparency mechanism users can verify.
3. Fair Points Program: Everyone starts at zero, no handicaps.
4. Market Making Vault: Protocol-run liquidity that handles liquidations.
5. Cross-collateral positions using vault deposits or borrow/lending balances.
6. Multi-asset coverage: Crypto + forex + synthetic stocks.

Extended note: Dedicated L1 Architecture & Multi-Asset Vision
Neony's architecture deserves a second mention. Building on a dedicated high-performance L1 - rather than deploying as a Solana program reflects an ambition to build purpose-built trading infrastructure at institutional throughput levels. 

The cross-collateral system, Market Making Vault design, and multi-asset roadmap (crypto + forex + stocks) indicate a team thinking in terms of a full-stack financial system, not just a DEX. This puts Neony in a different competitive tier than most perp DEX entrants.

Bullish Potential:
The post-FTX, post-insider-deal retail trader is a very real demographic. They're not going back to platforms that gave VCs 10x better entry prices. Neony's verifiable fairness is not a marketing claim - it's an on-chain property. That's a structural moat that compounds with every high-profile VC-backed launch that blows up.

2. @Tempo_Trade: Trading Automation 

Mission:
Hand trading is dying. Automation is the future.

Founded by @mejordev (MEV strategist, play-to-earn bot builder) and @SVMickey_ (Telegram bot developer, Solana specialist) - two traders who got tired of missing trades because humans are too slow.

Together they built systems trading across 5,000 tokens per day before they realized the real gap wasn't execution - it was accessible automation.

What Tempo does:
1. Auto buy/sell at preset price levels with auto-repeat
2. Grid trading across full price ranges
3. Copy trading for perpetuals (1-click follow top traders)
4. Strategy template sharing - you earn protocol fees when others use your template
5. Yield on idle capital via staking rewards while waiting for levels to hit
6. AI Setup Assistant: tell it what you want in plain English, it configures the strategy
7. Fully non-custodial - your funds never leave your wallet

Achievements:
1. Colosseum Eternal: Winner
2. Helius Redacted Hackathon: 2 tracks won
3. Sonic Mobius Hackathon: 1 track won
4. Colosseum Accelerator: Accepted
5 Poland Demo Day: Featured
6. Superteam Poland Grant: Recipient

Bullish Potential:
Trading bots already account for 50% of all Solana swap volume. Tokens now have an average lifespan of 72 seconds before the dump. No human can compete with that speed.

Tempo is building the automation layer for the next era of on-chain trading - and the fee-sharing template economy means every strategy creator becomes a growth engine for the protocol.

3. @derp_trade: Leverage + Prediction Markets
 
Mission:
Leverage any asset on Solana. Users stay in control of their funds.
Derp trade is a leverage trading and prediction market protocol with three distinct market types:
1. Coin markets: Standard on-chain token leverage
2. Kalshi-style event markets: Prediction market bets on real-world events
3. KOL markets: Leveraged positions on Key Opinion Leader performance

The KOL market is genuinely novel. It financialises influencer credibility on-chain, if you think a caller is going to pump tokens into the ground, you can bet on it. Transparency replaces opacity.

Liquidity providers "become the house", supplying capital to earn yield from protocol fees, with aligned incentives between the protocol and its capital base.

Bullish Potential:
Three markets in one. The multi-vertical architecture means Derp isn't exposed to any single narrative collapsing. 

The KOL market alone is a category that doesn't exist anywhere else in this form and the influencer economy in crypto is enormous, unaccountable, and waiting to be financialised.

4. @darklakefi: ZK Infrastructure + Privacy

Mission:
ZK is not just a privacy tool. It is the coordination layer for a new kind of network.

Darklake is the most technically ambitious project on this list.

Live products:
1. ZK-AMM on Solana mainnet: Private, confidential swaps
In development:
2. Perp DEX powered by ZK proofs: Institutional-grade privacy in derivatives
Core technology:
3. Zyga Protocol: Darklake's proprietary ZK technology stack

What Zyga enables:
1. Sub-second proof verification at Solana speed
2. Composable proofs: Chain, nest, and combine proofs for complex privacy apps
3. Encrypted on-chain application state
4. Cross-protocol ZK reasoning and verification
5. Reusable proofs across applications

The Zyga Protocol invention disclosure document has been published on the IACR cryptology preprint server (eprint . iacr . org / 2025 / 1802). This is not a fork of a popular ZK library. This is original research-grade cryptographic innovation.

Developer SDKs and comprehensive documentation are available, the team is explicitly positioning Zyga as infrastructure that other Solana protocols can integrate.

Bullish Potential:
MEV. Front-running. Transaction surveillance. These are not edge cases, they are the default experience of trading on a public blockchain. Darklake attacks these problems at the infrastructure layer. 

The IACR-published research, the live mainnet ZK-AMM, and the developer-first SDK approach all point to a team building a platform, not a point solution. First-mover advantage in ZK on Solana is a compounding moat.

5. @deloraprotocol: Cross-Chain Execution API

Mission:
One API for swaps and cross-chain flows across 20+ blockchains.

Delora is a B2B infrastructure protocol. It provides developers and protocols with a single unified API to access deep liquidity routing across more than 20 chains - without needing to build custom integrations for each.

OKX DEX - one of the largest routing engines across both Solana and EVM chains, is among Delora's integrated partners, providing immediate access to battle-tested, deep liquidity from day one.

The value proposition is simple: instead of your protocol team spending months building and maintaining cross-chain swap integrations, you call Delora's API and it's done.

Bullish Potential:
Multi-chain is inevitable. Every serious protocol will eventually need to route across Solana, Ethereum, Base, Arbitrum, and whatever L2s emerge next. Delora is the "picks and shovels" play, generating recurring B2B revenue where switching costs compound with every integration.

Infrastructure-layer businesses are historically among the most defensible in technology.

6. @XForgeOfficial: DePIN Hardware

Mission:
The ultimate DePIN phone. Purpose-built hardware for decentralised networks.

XForge is developing a smartphone designed from the ground up to participate in Decentralised Physical Infrastructure Networks (DePIN) on Solana.

General smartphones participating in DePIN face real friction: side-loaded apps that get killed by battery optimisation, background process restrictions, and hardware not optimised for continuous node participation.

XForge removes all of that friction. A dedicated device means uninterrupted node operation, purpose-built sensors and radios for DePIN protocol participation, and a hardware experience built around earning - not just consuming.

Users earn token rewards from Solana-based DePIN protocols simply by carrying or using their phone. The XForge Phone is the hardware entry point for mainstream DePIN adoption.

Context: Helium Mobile added 300,000 subscribers in Q1 2025 alone. DePIN is crossing into early majority territory. XForge arrives at exactly the right moment.

Bullish Potential:
The smartphone market is $500B+ per year. The DePIN sector on Solana is $3.5B market cap with 240,000 active nodes and growing.

A purpose-built device at the intersection of these two markets with an established Solana DePIN protocol ecosystem to integrate with from day one is a high-conviction convergence trade.

7. @outlight_ai: AI Trading Intelligence

Mission:
Transform social noise into actionable, trusted trade signals with integrated execution.

The Solana memecoin and token ecosystem generates an enormous volume of KOL (Key Opinion Leader) signals on X and Telegram every day. The problem: there is no accountability. Anyone can call a token, delete the post when it fails, and claim they only post alpha.
Outlight fixes this.

What it does:
1. Aggregates all public KOL signals from X and Telegram
2. Proof-of-call: Timestamps, contract addresses, first-call detection, deleted-post alerts
3. Scores every caller on: win-rate, average gain (with outlier capping), FDV at call time, signal velocity
4. Monty Score - composite KOL performance metric
5. Caller Style Classification, understand how a caller operates
6. Survival Rate, how many of their calls still have value after 7 days
7. Time-to-ATH tracking, when do their calls peak?
8. Signal Velocity Index, how fast do their calls move?
9. Most Called lists across 1h / 3h / 24h timeframes
10. In-platform trading with intelligent TP/SL presets
11. B2B WebSocket API for institutional clients

Bullish Potential:
Information asymmetry is the defining challenge of on-chain trading. Every trader knows the KOL economy is largely unaccountable noise, but they keep watching because occasionally the signal is real.

Outlight builds the trust and accountability layer that the entire ecosystem has been missing. The B2B API creates a second, higher-margin revenue stream. As data accumulates, signal quality improves and switching costs rise, a classic data network effect.

8. @sallar_io: DePIN Distributed Computing

Mission:
Your phone as a node. Distributed computing for the AI era.
Sallar is a DePIN computing protocol on Solana. Users share their device's idle GPU, CPU, and RAM via the Sallar app and earn tokens in return.
The network supports:
1. AI inference workloads
2. Big data processing
3. Cryptographic computation
4. Scientific research tasks

The Sallar Marketplace enables exchange of services and computing power. Sallar AI Agents, intelligent task automation services are also available within the ecosystem.

Bullish Potential:
The global AI compute market is growing faster than centralised supply can keep up with. Sallar democratises access to distributed compute via a mobile-first model that requires no expensive hardware just a phone people already own.

The deflationary tokenomics, Hacken audit, and fully-staffed executive team signal a project built for longevity, not a pump cycle.
